content:
Hi all, I’d like to ask whether a fully-verified floating-point layer would be in scope for CSLib, and how it should be factored if so.

I’m working on FloatSpec, a Lean 4 IEEE754 float formalization translated from Coq correspondence Flocq (using an autonomous agentic AI pipeline). It currently includes generic floating-point formats and rounding predicates, ulp reasoning, IEEE754-style encodings, executable reference operations, and error-bound scaffolding. I was recently told about the CSLib project, and it seems possible that FloatSpec could fit as a contribution.

Looking at CONTRIBUTING.md in cslib, my guess is that this would primarily fall under Pillar 1 as reusable CS infrastructure: supporting mathematics and semantics for floating-point arithmetic. I’m aware that there are already several related Lean efforts, so I want to clarify the intended difference and avoid duplication. My understanding is that Lean’s built-in Float/Float32 are mainly computational primitives rather than a reusable proof-level floating-point theory. TorchLean includes explicit Float32 / IEEE754-style semantics, but its main goal seems to be end-to-end neural-network execution and verification. By contrast, what I hope FloatSpec can provide is a more generic layer for reasoning about formats, rounding, ulp, IEEE754 encodings, and executable reference operations, which could potentially serve as shared infrastructure for later verified software / numerical verification developments.

I’m not proposing to upstream the repository as-is. The current branch still has 19 sorrys, and I’m working to eliminate them. If there is interest, I’d work towards preparing a CSLib-native PR with no sorrys and no new axioms. Before doing that, I wanted to ask:

  • Is this repo in scope for CSLib, or would it be better maintained as an external package?
  • How should this coordinate with existing Lean FP efforts to avoid duplication?

Thanks for your guidance, and since this is my first post on Zulip, please let me know if I should have posted this somewhere else or phrased anything differently :)

Hantao Lou said:

  • How should this coordinate with existing Lean FP efforts to avoid duplication?

I assume you're talking about https://juliahimmel.de/blog/float-qanda/ ? It recommends writing libraries externally and proving equivalence to their Float.Model.
Just FYI: #Project announcements > Flocq port

Thanks both!

@Jeremy Chen

Yes, that is partly what I had in mind. My understanding from Julia’s post is that external libraries should provide their own proof-oriented floating-point semantics, and then prove equivalence/compatibility with Float.Model where appropriate. That sounds very reasonable to me, especially since FloatSpec is closer to a Flocq-style real-valued semantics layer than to Lean’s runtime float model itself. Will try to target that in later versions of FloatSpec :)

@Ching-Tsun Chou

Thanks for the pointer! I had not noticed that thread before. This looks highly relevant to my work, and I have already started to follow up in that thread.

For a bit more context, I’m spending the summer at Berkeley Sky and would be very happy to contribute more to CSLib, either through direct repo-level contributions or by using auto-formalization to help scale CSLib development where that would be useful :)
